results.name: Fin.snocInduction
results.source_text:
/-- Recurse on a tuple by splitting into `Fin.elim0` and `Fin.snoc`. -/
@[elab_as_elim]
def snocInduction {α : Sort*}
    {motive : ∀ {n : ℕ}, (Fin n → α) → Sort*}
    (elim0 : motive Fin.elim0)
    (snoc : ∀ {n} (x : Fin n → α) (x₀), motive x → motive (Fin.snoc x x₀)) :
    ∀ {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → α), motive x
  | 0, x => by convert! elim0
  | _ + 1, x => snocCases (fun _ _ ↦ snoc _ _ <| snocInduction elim0 snoc _) x
results.docstring: Recurse on a tuple by splitting into `Fin.elim0` and `Fin.snoc`.

results.name: Physlib.List.takeWhile_orderedInsert'
results.source_text:
lemma takeWhile_orderedInsert' {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r]
    (a b : α) (hr : ¬ r a b) : (l : List α) →
    (List.takeWhile (fun c => !decide (r b c)) (List.orderedInsert r a l)).length =
    (List.takeWhile (fun c => !decide (r b c)) l).length
  | [] => by
    simp [List.orderedInsert, (Std.Total.total a b).resolve_left hr]
  | c :: l => by
    have hrba : r b a := (Std.Total.total a b).resolve_left hr
    simp only [List.orderedInsert]
    by_cases h : r b c
    · by_cases hac : r a c <;> simp [h, hac, hrba]
    · by_cases hac : r a c
      · exact absurd (IsTrans.trans _ _ _ hrba hac) h
      · simp only [hac, ↓reduceIte, h, decide_false, Bool.not_false, List.takeWhile_cons_of_pos,
        List.length_cons, add_left_inj]
        exact takeWhile_orderedInsert' r a b hr l

results.source_text:
/-- A definition of type `PositivityExt` tagged `@[positivity t]` extends the `positivity` tactic.
The term (with underscores) `t` indicates which expressions this extension accepts.
An extension will be given an expression `e : α`, together with hypotheses
`[Zero α] [PartialOrder α]` and attempts to prove `e > 0`, `e ≥ 0`, or `e ≠ 0`.

When `Positivity.core` calls this extension on an expression `e`, it does not guarantee that `e`
matches `t` perfectly: validate the form of the expression (using e.g.
`match_expr (← withReducible (whnf e))`) before building a proof. See also the
`let .app ... ← withReducible (whnf e) | throwError ...` lines in the example below.

An extension can call `Mathlib.Meta.Positivity.core` to recursively solve subgoals.

Example:
```lean
@[positivity ite _ _ _] def evalIte : PositivityExt where eval {u α} zα pα e := do
  let .app (.app (.app (.app f (p : Q(Prop))) (_ : Q(Decidable $p))) (a : Q($α))) (b : Q($α))
    ← withReducible (whnf e) | throwError "not ite"
  haveI' : $e =Q ite $p $a $b := ⟨⟩
  guard <| ← withDefault <| withNewMCtxDepth <| isDefEq f q(ite (α := $α))
  let ra ← core zα pα a; let rb ← core zα pα b
  ...
```
-/

results.name: Valuation.integer
results.source_text:
/-- The ring of integers under a given valuation is the subring of elements with valuation ≤ 1. -/
def integer : Subring R where
  carrier := { x | v x ≤ 1 }
  one_mem' := le_of_eq v.map_one
  mul_mem' {x y} hx hy := by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, map_mul, mul_le_one' hx hy]
  zero_mem' := by simp
  add_mem' {x y} hx hy := le_trans (v.map_add x y) (max_le hx hy)
  neg_mem' {x} hx := by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hx; simpa only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, map_neg]
results.docstring: The ring of integers under a given valuation is the subring of elements with valuation ≤ 1.

/-- Given two maps `s1` and `s2` whose targets carry an instance of an additive commutative
  monoid, the target of the sum of these two maps also carry an instance thereof. -/
instance : (i : ι1 ⊕ ι2) → AddCommMonoid ((fun i => Sum.elim s1 s2 i) i) := fun i =>
  match i with
  | Sum.inl i => inst1 i
  | Sum.inr i => inst2 i
